subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw introduce an operator-controlled way to retain custom headers such as x-api-key across cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and must that policy be scoped by destination origin instead of a global safe-header extension?
rationale: The request intentionally changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the trust model or acceptable guardrails.

options.title: Design a scoped operator policy
options.body: Allow the capability only with approved header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that preserve strict defaults.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and continue dropping credential-like custom headers on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add a global header extension list
options.body: Implement the requested shape directly, accepting the broader risk that an allowed header can be replayed to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Allow the capability only with approved header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, docs, and tests that preserve strict defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The current strict boundary traces to steipete's security-hardening commit, and this decision is about whether that boundary may be relaxed.
